title: DGT serial opening (bridge -> board, raw bytes)
description: Not a WebSocket frame: the exact bytes Arkab.Driver.DgtSerial writes to a single-board serial line when it opens it, on a line where nobody answers the bus ping (a single board, or a stand-in such as Arkab.Transport.Fake). Alnasl reads boards with this driver and its tests take these bytes apart, so they are pinned here as hex. bytes_hex is everything written, in order: probe_hex (to bus mode 0x4A, ping-all twice, end bus mode), then handshake_hex (reset 0x40, serial 0x45, version 0x4D, board 0x42, update mode: 0x4B nice with the clock, or 0x44 board only when the clock option is false), then asks_hex (0x41, one clock question, when the clock is wanted; empty when not). Nothing more is written until the first resync. A test reading these bytes should split them by the three parts, not by a hard-coded length.

clock.description: The driver's "clock" option (true unless set to false; the bridge always reads serial boards with the clock).
